nodes.Name: invalidTokenPanic
nodes.ValueLiteral: "invalid jsontext.Token; it has been voided by a subsequent json.Decoder call"

nodes.Name: Token
nodes.DocComment:
Token represents a lexical JSON token, which may be one of the following:
  - a JSON literal (i.e., null, true, or false)
  - a JSON string (e.g., "hello, world!")
  - a JSON number (e.g., 123.456)
  - a begin or end delimiter for a JSON object (i.e., { or } )
  - a begin or end delimiter for a JSON array (i.e., [ or ] )

A Token cannot represent entire array or object values, while a [Value] can.
There is no Token to represent commas and colons since
these structural tokens can be inferred from the surrounding context.

nodes.Name: Bool
nodes.DocComment: Bool constructs a Token representing a JSON boolean.

nodes.Name: String
nodes.DocComment:
String constructs a Token representing a JSON string.
The provided string should contain valid UTF-8, otherwise invalid characters
may be mangled as the Unicode replacement character.

nodes.Name: Float
nodes.DocComment:
Float constructs a Token representing a JSON number.
The values NaN, +Inf, and -Inf will be represented
as a JSON string with the values "NaN", "Infinity", and "-Infinity".

nodes.Name: Int
nodes.DocComment: Int constructs a Token representing a JSON number from an int64.

nodes.Name: Uint
nodes.DocComment: Uint constructs a Token representing a JSON number from a uint64.

nodes.Name: Clone
nodes.DocComment:
Clone makes a copy of the Token such that its value remains valid
even after a subsequent [Decoder.Read] call.

nodes.Name: Bool
nodes.DocComment:
Bool returns the value for a JSON boolean.
It panics if the token kind is not a JSON boolean.

nodes.Name: appendString
nodes.DocComment:
appendString appends a JSON string to dst and returns it.
It panics if t is not a JSON string.

nodes.Name: String
nodes.DocComment:
String returns the unescaped string value for a JSON string.
For other JSON kinds, this returns the raw JSON representation.

nodes.Name: appendNumber
nodes.DocComment:
appendNumber appends a JSON number to dst and returns it.
It panics if t is not a JSON number.

nodes.Name: Float
nodes.DocComment:
Float returns the floating-point value for a JSON number.
It returns a NaN, +Inf, or -Inf value for any JSON string
with the values "NaN", "Infinity", or "-Infinity".
It panics for all other cases.

nodes.Name: Int
nodes.DocComment:
Int returns the signed integer value for a JSON number.
The fractional component of any number is ignored (truncation toward zero).
Any number beyond the representation of an int64 will be saturated
to the closest representable value.
It panics if the token kind is not a JSON number.

nodes.Name: Uint
nodes.DocComment:
Uint returns the unsigned integer value for a JSON number.
The fractional component of any number is ignored (truncation toward zero).
Any number beyond the representation of an uint64 will be saturated
to the closest representable value.
It panics if the token kind is not a JSON number.

nodes.Name: Kind
nodes.DocComment:
Kind represents each possible JSON token kind with a single byte,
which is conveniently the first byte of that kind's grammar
with the restriction that numbers always be represented with '0':

  - 'n': null
  - 'f': false
  - 't': true
  - '"': string
  - '0': number
  - '{': object begin
  - '}': object end
  - '[': array begin
  - ']': array end

An invalid kind is usually represented using 0,
but may be non-zero due to invalid JSON data.

nodes.Name: String
nodes.DocComment: String prints the kind in a humanly readable fashion.

nodes.Name: normalize
nodes.DocComment: normalize coalesces all possible starting characters of a number as just '0'.
